sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Faidherbia albida, formerly Acacia albida, is an African savanna tree reaching about 30 m, with a spreading crown and bipinnate leaves. It often sheds leaves during the rainy season and retains them through the dry season.

sections.title: Flowers and pods
sections.text: Cream flowers grow in spikes. The thick orange pods are curved or coiled and can reach about 25–35 × 2–5 cm.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: The pods are mainly used as fodder; their flour and boiled seeds are also described as local foods. Sources do not always specify preparation, so these uses should not be extended to raw plant parts.
